# zutable

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/pedrobtz/zutable/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/pedrobtz/zutable/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![coverage](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pedrobtz/zutable/gh-pages/badges/coverage.svg)](https://github.com/pedrobtz/zutable/actions/workflows/coverage.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

zutable is a typed table for R: a data frame that knows each column's type,
queried through a bracket whose arguments are SQL's clauses.

- Every column has a logical type from [Apache Arrow](https://arrow.apache.org/docs/format/Columnar.html)
  and a nullability, and a query's result schema and type errors are known
  before any data is read.
- `:=` updates existing columns in place and never changes a table's
  schema.
- Grouping, sorting, joins and reductions run on a C kernel whose header
  other packages can use through `LinkingTo`.
- It imports no other package; [zufast](https://github.com/pedrobtz/zufast),
  on CRAN, is needed only to build it and is installed with it.

## Installation

Install the released version from CRAN:

``` r
install.packages("zutable")
```

Or the development version from GitHub:

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("pedrobtz/zutable")
```

## Usage

Build a table, then ask the bracket for the volume-weighted price of each
`id` after the first day:

```{r}
library(zutable)
trades <- zutable(
  id  = c(1L, 1L, 2L, 2L, 3L),
  day = as.Date("2026-01-01") + 0:4,
  px  = c(10.5, 11, 20, 19.5, 7),
  qty = c(100L, 50L, 10L, 30L, 200L)
)
trades[where = day >= "2026-01-02",
       select = .(vwap = sum(px * qty) / sum(qty)),
       by = id]
```

zutable also joins, updates in place, freezes and explains tables; Get
started shows each.

## Learn more

- [Get started](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zutable/articles/zutable.html):
  one table taken through a query, a type error, a join, an update and its
  plan.
- [Joins without surprises](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zutable/articles/joins.html):
  repeated keys, missing keys and key types.
- [Measuring the kernel](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zutable/articles/measurements.html):
  the kernel's timings against collapse, data.table and base R.
- The [reference index](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zutable/reference/index.html)
  lists every function.
